strategy.summary: Kugellager-Vertrieb Inntal is a sound Austrian family firm (founded 1981, 80 staff, equity ratio 43.4 %, stable credit index) that supplies two catalogue deep-groove bearings under framework agreement ctr:4600070640. It holds a 30 % quota on part:360020 and 60 % on part:360021, with sup:70620 as the second source on both. It is cheaper than the rival on both parts and has a perfect quality record over the last 12 months. Its delivery reliability is weak (86.5 % on time against a 95 % contract target). It has idle capacity: the second shift has been on hold since spring. It has also said openly that it is reviewing small accounts, and we are only about 0.3 % of its turnover. The renewal is open, and its first quote on 360020 is far above both its current price and anything its cost drivers support. The bearing producer-price index rose less than one percent and labour about three percent. Leverage is balanced. Our currency is volume and quota (fill the idle shift, look like a volume customer), not threats or rival prices. Aim for a flat or near-flat price on both parts, kept within the key account manager's own authority.
strategy.decision_maker: The key account manager decides price changes up to about 2 % alone. Anything above that goes to a pricing committee that meets every two weeks (doc:20260228-70640-M3, doc:20260512-70640-M2). The sales director sets account strategy and is currently reviewing small accounts (doc:20260819-70640-M1).

persona.style: Methodical and committee-bound. It asks high and settles well below its ask, alternating zero and moderate settlements. It asks for volume information and is account-portfolio minded.

It is reviewing small accounts. Our spend is about 0.3 % of its turnover.
Prices are fixed per calendar year, and changes need 90 days' notice before year end. The contract auto-extends unless notice is given by early April 2027.

price_view.reasoning: It already undercuts the rival on both parts, and the drivers support under one percent. The 360020 quote looks like pricing out a small account or reflects low benchmark volume, not cost. There is no should-cost, so evidence on its margin is thin. A realistic target is flat to a small rise, kept under its approval threshold, bought with volume and length. A deep cut is unlikely.

strategy.writer_notes: Open by answering its volume request: rising forecasts on both parts, plus a willingness to raise its share on the smaller-quota bearing and commit binding volume over a longer term. Then show that its cost indices justify almost no increase, and anchor at current prices. Bundle both bearings so we look like a volume customer. Keep moves small enough for the key account manager to approve without the committee. Never mention the rival's prices. Stay warm and reliable in tone.

findings.text: No should-cost exists for either bearing, so the margin over full cost cannot be measured. Price room has to be inferred from the index drivers, the price history and the quotes; on cost structure the evidence is thin.

The cost drivers justify almost nothing. PPI-C2815 (63-66% weight) rose +0.8% in 12 months and sits at its 36-month peak, only +3.7% above its low. LCI-C (9-12% weight) rose +2.7%. Weighted, that is about +0.8% on 360020 and about +0.9% on 360021.

Its new quote on 360020 is EUR 5.04, +20% on the current EUR 4.20. Nothing in the drivers supports that. It also sits far above the rival's 4.39 list/stock price and 4.63 RFQ quote. Either it is pricing out a small account (sales director, 2026-08-19) or the quote reflects the low benchmark volume.

Since 2023, 360020 has risen +3.4% (4.06 to 4.20, last change 2025). 360021 has risen +5.9% (6.81 to 7.21), including +4% from 2026-01. Over the same period PPI-C2815 rose only about 3.7% from its low, so 360021 has already outrun its cost drivers.

Its prices sit at or below the rival's: 4.20 against 4.39 on 360020, 7.21 against 7.23 on 360021. Earlier benchmarks match: it quoted 4.29 against 4.42 in 2025, and 7.15 against 7.42 in 2024. This leaves little room for a price cut; the realistic aim is to hold prices flat or allow at most about +1%.

The market news it may cite does not apply to ball bearings. Copper +48%, electronic boards +41% and steel +7.3% since January are not its weighted drivers. Power prices -43% since 2022 argue the other way.

findings.text: Decision structure: the key account manager can move up to 2 % alone; anything above 2 % goes to a pricing committee that meets every two weeks. This was repeated at two reviews (Feb and May 2026). Proposals at or below 2 % can close fast. Larger moves add two-week cycles, so we should plan the renewal calendar early.

Spare capacity: the second shift has been on hold since spring 2026, and sales twice offered to take additional parts at short notice (Feb and Jul). They need volume to fill capacity, which makes added or shifted volume (e.g. a higher quota on part:360020, now only 30 %) our strongest currency.

Red flag: the sales director said in Aug 2026 that they are reviewing small accounts and will focus on customers with volume. Our spend is about EUR 98k, roughly 0.3 % of their EUR 37 M turnover, so we risk being deprioritised or pushed to higher prices unless we bundle or raise volume.

Renewal request: they opened the renewal of ctr:4600070640 (part:360020, expires 30 June 2027) and asked for our expected volumes. They will present their offer in a meeting, so expect a volume-linked ask. Our forecast is up (28,600 vs 27,440 units; 17,330 vs 14,940 on part:360021) and has already been shared with suppliers.

Financially sound family firm: founded 1981, 80 staff, equity ratio 43.4 %, credit index stable at 180, VDA 6.3 grade A, ISO 9001 renewed. There is no financial stress and they could walk away, so a healthy-margin concern is low.

We pay them reliably: an average of 2.9 days after due, never more than 9 days late, and no unjustified discounts. They want faster payment (we are on 30 days against our standard of 60), which makes payment terms a tradeable item.
Evidence is thin. There is no news and no cost complaints in writing yet. Their likely cost argument is the bearings PPI at only +0.8 % plus labour at +2.7 %, which weakly supports any increase.

findings.text: Framework agreement ctr:4600070640 covers both bearings (6306-2Z C3 part:360020, 6308-2Z C3 part:360021), runs 2025-07-01 to 2027-06-30 and auto-extends 12 months unless terminated with 90 days' notice (by 2027-04-01). The supplier's e-mail of 2026-09-25 opens the renewal early. The exit is still open to us, but it is only credible because sup:70620 already supplies both parts.

Prices are fixed per calendar year. Any change needs written notice at least 90 days before year end, i.e. by about 2 Oct 2026 for 2027. A late or unannounced increase has no contractual footing for 1 Jan 2027.

Commercial terms: 30 days net (our standard is 60, so this already favours them), DAP with a 10-day lead time, quality agreement with a 95% on-time target and a EUR 150 flat fee per complaint. Delivery runs at 86.5% on time, below the target. Quality is 0 ppm, which is strong for them.

History: the supplier asks high and settles well below its ask. Averages are asked 3.2% vs settled 1.1% on 360020 and asked 4.5% vs settled 1.9% on 360021. Settlements alternate between 0% and moderate rises. 360021 rose 4.0% for 2026, so this year a zero is defensible. Settlements above 2% need their pricing committee, which meets every two weeks.

Dual sourcing with sup:70620 on both parts: 30/70 on 360020 and 60/40 on 360021. Both are standard catalogue bearings with no tooling on either side (tooling_owner n/a), so the library claim that the supplier owns tooling contradicts the sourcing records. Rival prices are higher: 4.39 vs 4.20 and 7.23 vs 7.21. Rival quotes are not a lever, since shifting quota would raise our cost.

Mutual dependency is low. Our spend of about EUR 98k is about 0.3% of their EUR 37M turnover, and they say they are reviewing small accounts. However, they have idle capacity (second shift on hold) and our forecast volumes are rising, so more volume or quota is the currency they value.

findings.text: Delivery is the main weakness: rolling 12 months 86.5% on time vs requested date (88.5% vs own confirmation) against the contractual 95% target; flat over two years (84-87%, dip to 80.8% in 2025Q4). When late, avg 10 days, max 21; part 360020 lateness is longer (13.3 days avg). Slightly above peer median 84.6%, so they will call it market-normal.

Quality argues their case: 0 complaints and 0 ppm in the last 12 months (peer median 457 ppm), down from 288-292 ppm in 2025. All 7 historic QNs were single pieces, 8Ds closed in 3-5 weeks, none overdue. Rival sup:70620 runs 299/335 ppm on the same parts. Do not lead on quality.
Defect cost to us is small: 7 complaints recharged at the EUR 150 flat fee (EUR 750 total); late-delivery cost is the larger performance cost item.

Volume outlook rises: part 360021 forecast 17,330 next 12m vs 14,940 ordered (+16%); part 360020 28,600 vs 27,440 (+4%). Forecasts shared with supplier. Their share: ~8.2k of 360020 (30% quota) and ~9k of 360021 (60%). With spare capacity (second shift on hold) and a stated focus on volume customers, quota shift is our main lever.

Price: they are cheaper than the rival on both parts (360020 4.20 vs 4.39; 360021 7.21 vs 7.23), so rival prices help them. Prices rose 3.4%/5.9% since 2023; ordering is clean (0 stale/rush on 360020, 1-2 on 360021).

arguments.text: We are already the cheaper source on both bearings and the better one on quality. On 360020 we are at 4.20 against 4.39 from Wälzlager-Zentrum Süd. On 360021 we are at 7.21 against 7.23. We have had zero complaints in the last 12 months, against 299 and 335 ppm at the rival. Moving volume to us lowers Hollerau's total cost even if our price rises a little.

Our prices on 360020 have lagged costs. The price was flat in 2024 and flat again in 2026, so it has risen only 3.4 % since 2023. Over the same period labour rose 10.9 % from its low and steel is up 7.3 % since January. The rival itself has moved from 4.12 to 4.39, and its 2026-09 benchmark quote was 4.63.

A 30 % share at about 8,000 pieces a year is a small account for us. We are reviewing small accounts, so the price has to reflect the effort of serving a small volume. The rival's 4.39 offer is list price, from stock only, and valid for just 7 days.
Hollerau pays late habitually: 84.7 % of invoices are paid after the due date. That late payment carries a cost for us.

weak_points: Our 5.04 quote on 360020 is 20 % above our current price. The bearing producer-price index rose only 0.8 % in 12 months, so the quote cannot be defended on cost.
Our on-time delivery is 86.5 % against the 95 % target in the contract.
We have told them twice that our second shift is idle and that we could take more parts at short notice. They know we need volume.
Changes above 2 % need our pricing committee, and they know this too.
Copper and electronic boards are not relevant to bearings. Power prices are down 43 %.
We cited no real cost data and have no should-cost to show.
The contract extends automatically and prices are fixed per year. To change the 2027 price we must give notice 90 days before year end.
wants: A higher quota on 360020, from 30 % to 50-70 %.
Binding annual volumes: about 14-20k pieces of 360020 and 17k pieces of 360021.
On-time payment, or payment terms under 30 days.
In return for the above I can offer 0-2 % or flat prices, kept within the key account manager's own authority.
red_lines: No price cut below the current 4.20 / 7.21.
No 2027 price freeze while the quota stays at 30 % with no commitment.
No penalties tied to the 95 % on-time delivery target unless volume is raised.
red_team.opening: I will open warmly: we value the partnership, and they can see our zero-defect record and our competitive pricing. I will ask for the expected volumes first. Then I will present 360020 at about 4.65 and 360021 at about 7.45, with the cost argument based on labour and steel. Early on I will signal that a larger share and a 2-3 year commitment would let us stay close to our current prices.

rebuttals.answer: We agree, and we value it: your price on both bearings is competitive and your quality over the last year has been excellent, which we gladly acknowledge. That is exactly why we want to give you more of our growing need rather than less. But that only works at a price that stays competitive. A rise that erodes your advantage would remove the very reason to shift volume your way. Our proposal is to grow your share and commit binding volume at stable prices, so both sides keep the benefit you describe.

The cost index for bearings and driving elements, which makes up most of this part's cost, has barely moved over the last year, and labour, a small share, adds only a fraction of a percent on the price. Steel's basic producer price is not the same as the price of a finished catalogue bearing, and the bearing index already reflects it. Your price on this part has also risen since we started, and in past renewals we found fair middle ground. What the cost evidence supports is close to zero, far from the quote you sent.

We understand you are focusing on customers with volume, and we want to be one of them. Our forecast for both bearings is rising and has been shared with you; taken together the two parts are a meaningful, steady flow. You have told us you have spare capacity and could take more parts at short notice, so additional volume from us fills capacity you already have rather than adding effort. We are ready to raise your share on the smaller-quota bearing and commit volume over a longer term, which answers the small-account concern directly.

You are right that our payments often land a few days after due, and we will work on paying on time. In proportion, the delay is a matter of days, never beyond ten days, with no discounts deducted and no short payments over the whole relationship. Your terms are also already much shorter than our standard. We are happy to commit to punctual payment as part of the renewal, but a few days' delay does not justify a price increase.

press: We would be grateful if you could help us understand how the new quote for the smaller bearing relates to the bearing cost index, which has moved only slightly over the past year.
With the additional volume we have in mind, we would like to agree together how deliveries can reach the on-time target set out in our agreement.
Since you mentioned capacity to take additional parts at short notice, we would like to explore how a larger, binding share could keep prices stable for both bearings.
We would appreciate a proposal for both bearings together that your key account team can confirm directly, so we can conclude the renewal smoothly.
As prices under our agreement are fixed per calendar year, we suggest we keep the current prices in place while we settle the terms for the new period.
